## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fcee8b8404e83cb5136fc121e6aa73e32f5856db`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .github/workflows/fleet-write.yml + none (the code the comment cites, `scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs` and `ops.mjs` on this head, is outside the diff: read to judge, not reviewed)

### ① Derived judgments

- Face and tier: the PR's file list is one path, `.github/workflows/fleet-write.yml`; `GOVERNED_SURFACES` row `workflows` (`.github/workflows/**`, Tier H, `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` L1214) matches it, so `reviewFace` returns the `rules` face, tier name `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. No schema suspect, no changeset in the tree. Head repo `objectstack-ai/objectstack`, not a fork; draft; labels `ci/cd`, `size/s`, `skip-changeset`; no assignees.
- Net diff against `main` (merge-base `a40eb02e8`, one commit `fcee8b840`): one file, +9/-8, one hunk at L154–L162. Stripping every `#` line from the diff leaves zero changed lines: no key, value, `permissions:`, `if:`, `run:`, `uses:` or step moved. Read with whitespace normalised, the removed and added text differ only in the three sentences the card orders (FOUR → FIVE with `advisory_versions` added to the list; the one-read sentence → a two-read sentence naming `advisory_read` and `advisory_list`; "its stroke" → "either's stroke"); the measurement sentence (2026-11-02, run 41415522766), the ⚠️ EXPECTED paragraph and the ⛔ refused-mint sentence are byte-identical after the re-wrap. None of the three cited files changed on `origin/main` (`3c380253e`) since the merge-base, and `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main pr-31468` exits 0.
- Every factual claim in the new comment, checked against `ops.mjs` and `validate.mjs` on this head:
  - "FIVE write consumers": `ops.mjs` rows `advisory_report` (L2502), `advisory_create` (L2520), `advisory_collaborators_add` (L2542), `advisory_versions` (L2554), `advisory_state` (L2572) each carry `permission: 'repository-advisories'`, `alone: true` and no `grant`, so `levelOf` (`validate.mjs` L514, `OPS[op].grant ?? PERMISSIONS[OPS[op].permission]`) resolves to `PERMISSIONS['repository-advisories']` = `'write'` (`ops.mjs` L2110). The card's "FOUR" was stale: `advisory_versions` landed after the sentence was written, and the order said recount, not copy. Five is right.
  - "`advisory_collaborators_add`, `advisory_versions` and `advisory_state` (one advisory's PATCH)": `verb: 'PATCH'` on `/repos/${repo}/security-advisories/${a.ghsa_id}` at L2547, L2561–L2562, L2577. "one private report": `POST .../security-advisories/reports` (L2509–L2510). "one draft advisory": `POST .../security-advisories` (L2527–L2528).
  - "one at a time ... travels alone": `alone: true` on all seven advisory rows; `strokeErrors` (`validate.mjs` L517–L528) refuses a stroke carrying an `alone` op beside anything else, and the self-test row at L1749 pins `alone` on all seven.
  - "the validator writes `permission_repository_advisories=write` for it and an EMPTY value for every other stroke": `tokenPermissionsOf` (L585–L597) plus the output writer; self-test L1847–L1848 asserts `permission_repository_advisories=write` for each writing row's stroke, L1863 asserts `permission_repository_advisories=` and no such grant for every other op alone and for the shared-token stroke of them all, L1375 asserts the empty line in the real `--from-event --github-output` output for a comment.
  - "TWO read consumers ... `advisory_read` (one advisory's GET) and `advisory_list` (the collection's GET, the listing)": `advisory_read` L2584, `grant: 'read'` L2586, `GET /repos/${repo}/security-advisories/${a.ghsa_id}` L2591; `advisory_list` L2598, `grant: 'read'` L2600, `GET /repos/${repo}/security-advisories` L2605; both `alone: true`. The spelling "the collection's GET" matches the path: the collection endpoint, no id.
  - "writes `permission_repository_advisories=read` for either's stroke, never `write`": self-test L2003 (a read's stroke) and L2085 (a listing's stroke) both assert `permission_repository_advisories=read` and a token map with `'repository-advisories': 'read'`; the header (L132–L136) states the same for both rows; L1864 pins that exactly the seven rows spend `repository-advisories` and nothing else does.
  - "the same way as `permission-actions`": `STROKE_SCOPED_PERMISSIONS` = `['actions', 'repository-advisories']` (`ops.mjs` L2126); `validate.mjs` L1304–L1310 pins that the workflow reads each as `${{ steps.validate.outputs.permission_NAME }}` (the grant's name with `-` as `_`) and nothing else that way.
- Pins and censuses. `git grep` on the head tree for `FOUR write consumers`, `write consumers`, `one advisory's GET`, `advisory_read`, `advisory_list` and `advisory_versions` under `scripts/**` and `.github/**`: no script reads any changed sentence. The readers of `fleet-write.yml`'s text in `validate.mjs` (L1304–L1310 `permission-*` inputs; L1429–L1432 `repositories:` and `owner:`; L1599–L1601 the `permission-actions` output line and the absence of `run_rerun_failed` / `rerun-failed-jobs`; L1709–L1715 step env, `client_payload`, `run:` lines; L1866–L1869 the `permission-repository-advisories` output line, no literal level, the `Unexpected input(s) 'permission-repository-advisories'` literal, one mint step) read non-comment lines or a literal this diff leaves byte-for-byte; L1712 filters `#` lines out explicitly. The hits in `dispatch.mjs` and `check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` are that code's own comments and tables about the ops, not reads of the workflow text. Nothing had to move.
- Order compliance: comment text only (held), recounted write consumers (held, FIVE), `Fixes #31447`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body (held), `skip-changeset` label (held), `check-governed-merges` and `dispatch-gates --tier` verdicts in the body (present: GOVERNED, Tier H, no model mandate), root `ci.yml` and `ui/.github/**` untouched (held). Commit trailer model-free per the standing lines.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: a workflow file, published by no package; `Check Changeset` on this head is `success`. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` hold, since no published spec or metadata surface changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Follow-up, not a blocker (confirmed): `validate.mjs` L574–L584, `tokenPermissionsOf`'s doc comment, still names `advisory_read` alone as the row that "adds `repository-advisories: read`", while the file's own header (L134–L136) and the self-test at L2085 name `advisory_list` beside it. Doc comment only, nothing reads it; the order kept `scripts/**` out of this card's surface unless a pin read the workflow text, and none does. One-line fix on a later card.
- Follow-up, not a blocker (confirmed): the comment above `permission-actions` (`fleet-write.yml` L145) says "ONE consumer: the `workflow_dispatch` row", but `run_rerun_failed` (`ops.mjs` L2489, `permission: 'actions'` L2490, `alone: true` L2493, no `grant`, so `write`) spends the same input; `validate.mjs`'s header L129–L130 says so ("for a `workflow_dispatch` or `run_rerun_failed` stroke"). The self-test pin at L1601 ("ruling 3, no workflow edit") asserts the workflow text contains neither `run_rerun_failed` nor `rerun-failed-jobs`, so a corrected comment must count two consumers without naming the second op or its path (the header's own phrasing, "the workflow names neither op", shows the intended shape). Pre-existing, out of this card's ruling; carried as the dev reported it.
- Deviations in the dev report (one `gh api` GET for read-back, the harness PR-body footer, a stray empty file at the container root outside the repo, FOUR not copied): read; none touches the diff or the contract. Accepted.
- Tests "none owed": correct for a comment-only workflow change; no ablation is owed.

### ④ Design judgment

The change does what the ruling says and nothing more: the comment above the one stroke-scoped advisories input now names every row that spends it, at the level each spends it, and the counts it states (five at `write`, two at `read`) are the counts the op table and the validator's self-test pin on this head. The sentence structure keeps the load-bearing facts a reader of the workflow needs without opening the scripts: which strokes mint the grant, that each travels alone, that every other stroke gets an EMPTY value, and that the two reads never mint `write`. The measured-run sentence and the EXPECTED-warning paragraph, which a self-test literal depends on, are untouched. No key or value moves, so the minted token's shape is unchanged on every stroke; worst case is nil at runtime. No must-fix, no should-fix on the diff; the two follow-ups above are nits on neighbouring comments outside the file surface.

Check-runs on fcee8b840, read at 2026-11-08T09:53Z: 57 runs, 20 `success`, 16 `skipped` (opt-in and matrix placeholders), 0 `failure`, 21 still `in_progress` (the 16 `Test UI` shards, `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, and the root lanes `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · source gates`), not waited on. `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Type Check · workspace` and `Type Check · debt ledger` are `success`. Tier H: the landing is the maintainer's merge or enqueue, or an authorized APPROVED review and then the owning seat lands it; this record does not lift that.
